name: Omni Homestead
insider_take: America's first resort destination where presidents have soaked and socialites have played for over 250 years.
whats_special: The Omni Homestead sits on natural hot springs that have been drawing visitors since 1766, making it one of America's oldest resorts. The property features its own ski slopes, championship golf courses designed by Robert Trent Jones Sr., and the famous Jefferson Pools - outdoor spring-fed pools where Thomas Jefferson himself once bathed. The resort spans 2,000 acres in Virginia's Allegheny Mountains and maintains much of its original Georgian architecture.
pro_tip: Book a treatment at the spa that incorporates the mineral-rich spring water, and time your visit for the fall foliage season when the surrounding Blue Ridge Mountains create a spectacular backdrop.
dont_miss: A soak in the legendary Cascades Gorge, falconry demonstrations on the Great Lawn, and a round of golf on the Old Course where Sam Snead learned to play. The resort's afternoon tea service and historic casino (America's oldest) are also quintessential Homestead experiences.
pros: Historic grand resort with over 250 years of hospitality tradition
Natural hot springs and world-class spa facilities
Championship golf courses including the Cascades Course
Extensive outdoor activities including skiing, hiking, and horseback riding
cons: Remote mountain location requires travel planning
Premium pricing reflects luxury resort status
